Indian Standard

SPECIFICATION FOR NYLON MONOFILAMENTS
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 2 August 1963, after the draft finalized by the Brushware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Nylon is now extensively used in the manufacture of monofilaments for brushes. Although other materials are also used, yet nylon monofilaments are being increasingly used in place of bristles. Amongst other attributes, nylon monofilaments are easy to wash and have, therefore, been found popular for tooth brushes, hair brushes, nail brushes, and other toilet and industrial brushes. 0.2.1 The diameter of nylon monofilaments is chosen to suit the end use, but the range varies generally from 0.15 to 0.60 mm. 0.2.2 Three basic types of nylon ( polyamides ), namely, nylon 610, 66 and 6 are generally used in the manufacture of nylon monofilaments intended for use as filling material for brushes. Nylon 610 is a linear polycondensation product of a 6-carbon diamine and lo-carbon ( sebacic ) acid; nylon 66 is a linear polycondensation product of a 6-carbon diamine and 6-carbon ( adipic ) acid, whereas nylon 6 is an internal condensation product of hexamethylene diamine ( caprolactum ). -Both nylon 6, and to a greater extent, nylon 66 are largely used in the manufacture of nylon monofilaments. Nylon 6 10 is, however, not consumed to the same extent because it is more expensive. All these types of nylons are not manufactured indigenously but are imported in hermetically sealed tins, which are only opened at the time of manufacture. However, in the near future manufacturing of the three types of nylon is also likely to come up. 0.2.3 Indigenous production of nylon monofilaments dates back to 1959. The total consumption of this material within the country has been met and export markets in neighbouring Asian and African countries may be attempted in the near future. 0.3 Realizing the growing importance of nylon monofilaments in the brushware industry, the Sectional Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard agreed to lay down the basic requirements of this material in a national standard. Thts specification is, therefore, being issued and it is intended to serve as a guide in assisting manufacturers to upgrade the 3

quality of the mat&al currently produced and also to aid brush manufacturers in selecting material of acceptable quality. 0.4 Wherever a reference to any Indian Standard appears in thii specification, it shall be taken as a refaence to the latest version of the standard. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with ' IS : Z-1960 Rules for Rounding Off Numerical Values ( Revised). The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specifkd value in this standard. 0.6 This standard is intended chid to cover the technical provisions relating to nylon monofilaments an J it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract. . 1. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Appearance -The nylon monofilaments shall be cylindrical and smooth. They shall not be wavy or twisted and shall be free from ovalness and indentations. 3.2 Physico-Chemical Requirements - The nylon monofilaments shall comply with the requirements given in Table I. 4. PACKING AND MARKING

4.1 Packing -The nylon monofilaments shall be packed in rolla hygienically, prefixably in transparent plastic sleevings which hold the filaments in a straight form and which are non-toxic and do not attract dirt. 4

4.3 The rolls containing nylon monofilaments shall be packaged in lots of 25 kg or 50 kg in cardboard boxes. ' A package may contain rolls of either of these lengths or both together. following information shall be legibly and indelibly 4.5 Marking -The marked or stamped on each roll or package : a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, if any; b) The net weight of the material when packed; and c) Type and gauge. 4.5.1 The rolls may also be marked with the IS1 Certification Mark.

NOTE -The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard made thereunder. conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control, which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. The IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a liccnce for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processon, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. ,

METHODS

6.1 Tests shall be carried out as prescribed in the ielevant appendices to this standard. 6.2 Qpality of Reagents - Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals ( see Note ) and distilled water [ SCG IS : 1070-1960 Specification for Water, Distilled Quality ( Revised ) ] shall be employed in tests.
NOTE- `Pure chemic?ls' shall mean chemicals which do not contain impurities which alTectthe results of anal@. 6.3 Identification Test - The three types of nylon monofilaments be distinguished by the following tests.

shall

Boil the nylon monofilaments in hydrochloric acid bf 4-2 N. Only monofilaments of nylon 6 10 will remain undissolved, whereas nylon 66 and 6 dissolve. 6.3.2 Colour Test - This is a rapid identification distinguishing monofilaments of nylon 66 from nylon 6. test used for

their differential solubility in hydrochloric acid solution of a definite strength.

6.3.1 Solsrbility Test -

Distinguish nylon 610 from nylon 66 and 6 by

Immerse the nylon monofilaments in a solution prepared by mixing the following: Phenol Lactic acid, 75 percent Glycerol Water saturated with either cereus blue or cotton blue 10 g 10 g 20 g 22ml .

After immersion for 30 to 45 seconds, wash free of the coloured solution. Nylon 6 monofilaments shall appear deeply coloured z&d considerably swollen. Nors -The colour testir not applicable to coloured fikneats in which case tbc density and melting point values ahall be employed for identikmtion. 6

D
ABSORPTION

[ Table I, Sl No. (iv)]

D-l.1 Weigh accurately 0.5 to ! g of nylon monofilaments in a clean and dry weighing bottle and dry at 105 to 110�C to constant weight. Transfer this quantity of nylon monofilaments in a 250-ml beaker containing water and keep them immersed for 24 hours. At the end of this period remove the nylon monofilaments, dry them in the folds of a filter paper and weigh. D-2. APPENDIX ( czuuse 5.1 )

E

SAMPLING OF NYLON MONOFILAMENTS CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY El. LOT

E-1.0 In any consignment, all the nylon monofilaments of the same type, gauge and belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together into 100 rolls or less and each such group shall constitute a lot. . E-l.1 The conformity of the nylon monofilaments in a lot to the requirements of this specification shall be ascertained for each lot separately. Five rolls shall be selected for this purpose from each of the lots. E-l.2 The rolls shall be selected at random If the rolls in a bottom portions of the box. one box, approximately equal number of rolls from as many boxes as possible so as to obtain E2. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA from the top, middle and lot are packed in more than shall be selected at random a total of 5 rolls. FOR CONFORMITY

E-2.1 From each of the rolls selected according to E1.2, an equal number of strands of nylon monofilaments shall be pulled out with the help of a metal sampler. The strands thus obtained shall be pooled together, for density ( see Appendix C) and water-absorption determinations (see Appendix D ). E2.1.1 The results of density and water-absorption determinations shall satisfy the requirements given in Table I, before further tests as given in E2.2 and E2.3 are carried out. E-2.2 From each of the remaining portions of the selected rolls, required quantities of strands shall be chosen and shall be separately tested for melting point ( see Appendix B ). 10

-Is11843-1963 E-2.2-1 The lot shall be considered as satisfying the specification requirement for melting point if4 out of 5 test results obtained according to E2.2 are found satisfactory.
E-2.3 Four strands of nylon monofilaments shall be picked up at random from each of the still remaining portions of the 5 selected rolls so as to obtain a total of 20 strands. These 20 strands of nylon monofilaments shall be measured, for the gauge requirements ( see Appendix A ). E2.4 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of the specification, if the stipulations laid down in E-2.1 to E2.3 are all fulfilled. .
